I am 70 years old and I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I finished high school, so I do my own calculations and I read the nutrient contents on the fertilizer bags. My wife and I are the only laborers, and we irrigate from our own well with an electric pump. Our soil is loamy alluvial land from the old Yellow River course — it is fairly fertile but drains fast, so I must replace nitrogen every season.

I keep 5 mu in my cabbage-maize-spinach rotation, and I use 0.5 mu on the south field edge for chili and 0.5 mu near the well house for kidney bean. That uses all 6 mu.

For the spring cabbage on the 5 mu, I will plant hybrid Jinbai 87. Last year I got 7,500 kg per mu but the heads were a bit loose, so this year I will increase the nitrogen by one extra urea topdressing. I will rotary till the ground first, spreading 100 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as basal dressing, then topdress twice with 10 kg per mu of urea each time. That works out to 25 kg nitrogen, 12 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate 4 times: right after transplanting, at rosette stage, at early heading, and at full heading. I will spray pesticide 6 times total — 4 times for cabbage worm and aphids, 2 times for soft rot. I expect 8,000 kg per mu.

After I harvest cabbage in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize on the same 5 mu. I use hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. I plant no-tillage because saving those 5 days between crops matters — if I plant late, the frost comes before the grain fills. I apply 80 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at sowing, which is 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once at jointing and once at grain filling. I spray 3 times: once with herbicide before emergence, twice with insecticide for Asian corn borer. I expect 1,100 kg per mu.

After maize harvest in early October, I plant winter spinach on the same 5 mu. I use an improved variety. I apply 80 kg per mu of compound fertilizer plus 5 kg per mu of urea — that is 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I rotary till lightly. I irrigate twice because winter rainfall is low on the North China Plain. I spray 5 times: 3 times for aphids, 2 times for downy mildew. I expect 4,500 kg per mu.

For the 0.5 mu of chili, I plant an improved variety in May. I apply 90 kg per mu of compound fertilizer and 10 kg per mu of urea — 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 12 kg potassium per mu. I rotary till, irrigate 4 times, and spray 20 times because chili gets anthracnose and thrips badly in this humidity. I expect 5,500 kg per mu.

For the 0.5 mu of kidney bean, I plant traditional seed I saved from last year. I apply 80 kg per mu of compound fertilizer — 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. I rotary till, irrigate 5 times, and spray 10 times for pod borer and rust. I expect 5,000 kg per mu.

I have done the cost sums. Cabbage is my main cash crop so it gets the most fertilizer. Maize gets less because the grain price is only 0.8 yuan per kg, so the margin is thinner. I would rather add an extra 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu than risk a bad harvest — losing a cabbage crop costs me 3,000 yuan per mu, but extra fertilizer costs only 60 yuan. My neighbor Lao Zhang uses almost the same rates, and I watch his fields. If his yields are better, I will ask him what he changed and try it on half a mu next year. We are both getting older, so I hire the rotary tiller driver for 40 yuan per mu instead of doing it by hand. Every yuan counts when there are only two of us.
